blocks.text: The fiery watcher stayed outside the laboratory window. Perch was fighting the tank, and every angry turn sent another surge through the robot’s cables. Daniel smiled at the rising meter.
The fiery watcher drew nearer the glass. Inside, Perch’s glow pulsed through the water, then into the cables.

The watcher moved toward the tank, then stopped at the laboratory window. There was no way to lift the locked tank with a face and flame; getting close would put heat against the glass and water. He turned toward the city to find help.
Near dawn, Seth was already on his way to Billy’s office. He had slept badly. Every time he closed his eyes, he saw Perch pressed against the bars of the intake.

Jenny was there before him, bringing a proof of the Defender’s morning story. It challenged Daniel’s cleanup claim and described the attack and the extraction device. Billy read beside his desk while Fist hovered at the window.
Then Fist backed away from it. “We’ve got company.”
An orange glow lit the glass. Seth stepped closer. A face hovered beyond the window.
Billy opened the window. A ball of fire drifted inside and stopped above the sill. Its flames flickered over an anxious face. Billy stepped back from the curtains.
“I’m Flaming Head,” the newcomer said.
Seth heard the words clearly. Jenny lifted her eyes at the same moment. Billy looked from one to the other.
“What does he want?” Billy asked.
Seth realized Billy had seen the face move but heard nothing he could understand. He repeated the name.
Flaming Head looked at Seth, then Jenny. “You both need to hear this. Orkleson has the fish.”
Seth felt his stomach drop. “Perch? We got him out.”
“They caught him again,” Flaming Head said. “He’s in a tank inside the robot. Orkleson’s taking it into the city.”
Seth told Billy and Fist what he was hearing. Jenny needed no explanation. She had gone pale.
“Wait,” Seth said. He looked at Flaming Head, then at her. “Why Jenny?”
Jenny clasped her hands and looked down. Flaming Head’s glow lit the office while Seth waited, confused. Billy lowered the newspaper proof.
blocks.alt: Flaming Head reveals himself in Billy’s office as Jenny shyly admits she was changed by the lake blast.

blocks.text: “I was jogging there that night,” she said quietly. “The wave hit me. Afterward, I could run… much faster than I should.”
Seth remembered Jenny stepping clear of the bicycle before Billy could warn her, and answering Perch’s cry at the cage.
“You heard him,” he said.
Jenny nodded. “I didn’t know how to explain it. I was still trying to understand it myself.”
Seth let go of the chair back. He wasn’t the only one who had been trying to explain this.
Flaming Head lowered himself nearer the desk. “I’m what fell into the water.”
“That was you?” Seth said.
“The crash scattered my energy,” Flaming Head said. “You, Jenny, the fish—you were in its path. I didn’t know what it would do.”
“Why didn’t you come sooner?” Jenny asked. “I saw the damaged shore,” Flaming Head said. “I thought I’d hurt everyone I touched. I thought you’d drive me away.”
Jenny shook her head. “We need you here.”
“Then I saw you lift the tree,” he told Seth. “The man underneath it lived. I hadn’t only done harm.”
“You were there?” Seth asked. “I felt warm.” “I stayed close. I was going to leave, until they caught Perch.”
Jenny glanced at the laboratory sketch. “Could you get him out?” “I couldn’t grip the tank. My heat would hurt him before I could break it. I need your hands.”
“Daniel’s using what came from me to hurt people,” Flaming Head said. “I can’t leave while Perch is in that machine.”
Jenny looked toward the brightening window. “Does Daniel know?”
“He knows the fish can power his machine. That’s enough to hurt him.”
Seth repeated the warning for Billy. The detective set the proof aside. A story exposing Daniel would not stop a robot already on its feet.
“We know where he is,” Billy said. “First we plan how to get that tank out.”
Fist moved toward the open window. Seth stood so quickly he caught his knee on the desk. Jenny steadied him, then gave him a small, nervous smile.
He looked at Flaming Head. “You’ll help us get Perch out?”
The flames rose around the little face. “That’s why I came.”
Billy cleared a space on his desk. “Then tell us what you saw.” Seth pulled up a chair beside Jenny while Flaming Head hovered over the paper.
